name: Semaglutide
averageWeightLoss: ~15% body weight over 68 weeks (Wegovy 2.4mg, STEP 1 trial). Ozempic shows ~6-10% weight loss at diabetes doses.
administration: Subcutaneous injection (Ozempic, Wegovy) or Oral tablet (Rybelsus)
approvedFor: Ozempic: Type 2 Diabetes; Wegovy: Weight Management; Rybelsus: Type 2 Diabetes (oral)
mechanism: Semaglutide mimics the naturally occurring hormone GLP-1, binding to GLP-1 receptors in the pancreas to stimulate insulin secretion and suppress glucagon release in a glucose-dependent manner. It also slows gastric emptying and acts on hypothalamic receptors to reduce appetite and food intake, leading to significant weight loss.
titrationSchedule: Wegovy: Start at 0.25mg weekly for 4 weeks, increase to 0.5mg for 4 weeks, then 1mg for 4 weeks, then 1.7mg for 4 weeks, then maintenance dose of 2.4mg weekly. Ozempic: Start at 0.25mg weekly for 4 weeks, increase to 0.5mg, may increase to 1mg or 2mg after at least 4 weeks. Rybelsus: Start at 3mg daily for 30 days, increase to 7mg, may increase to 14mg after at least 30 days.
seriousRisks: Thyroid C-cell tumors (observed in rodent studies; relevance to humans unknown)
Acute kidney injury (usually secondary to dehydration from GI side effects)
Diabetic retinopathy complications (in patients with existing retinopathy)
Hypoglycemia (when used with insulin or sulfonylureas)
Suicidal ideation (under FDA investigation, no causal link established)
contraindications: Personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC)
Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia syndrome type 2 (MEN 2)
Known hypersensitivity to semaglutide or any excipients
History of serious hypersensitivity reaction to semaglutide
insuranceCoverage: Often covered for Type 2 Diabetes (Ozempic). Coverage for weight management (Wegovy) varies widely by plan; many commercial plans now cover it but Medicare Part D does not cover weight loss medications. Prior authorization typically required.
halfLife: ~7 days (injection); ~1 week apparent half-life (oral, due to absorption-limited kinetics)
clinicalTrials: STEP program (weight management: STEP 1-5, SELECT cardiovascular outcomes trial), SUSTAIN program (Type 2 Diabetes: SUSTAIN 1-10), PIONEER program (oral semaglutide: PIONEER 1-10)

keyResults.step1: 16.9% average weight loss vs 2.4% placebo over 68 weeks
keyResults.select: 20% reduction in major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in overweight/obese adults without diabetes
keyResults.sustain6: 26% reduction in MACE in Type 2 Diabetes patients

keyAdvantages: Most widely studied GLP-1 RA for weight management
keyDisadvantages: GI side effects common during titration
Injection required for weight loss doses
Ongoing supply constraints
High cost without insurance
Weight regain common after discontinuation

name: Tirzepatide
averageWeightLoss: ~22.5% body weight over 72 weeks at 15mg dose (SURMOUNT-1 trial). Diabetes doses (Mounjaro) show ~12-15% weight loss.
approvedFor: Mounjaro: Type 2 Diabetes; Zepbound: Weight Management
mechanism: Tirzepatide is a first-in-class dual incretin agonist that activates both GLP-1 and GIP (glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide) receptors. GLP-1 activation stimulates insulin secretion, suppresses glucagon, slows gastric emptying, and reduces appetite. GIP activation enhances insulin sensitivity and may improve fat metabolism. The dual mechanism produces greater weight loss and glycemic control than GLP-1 agonists alone.
titrationSchedule: Start at 2.5mg weekly for 4 weeks (initiation dose, not therapeutic), increase to 5mg weekly. May increase by 2.5mg increments every 4 weeks based on response and tolerability. Maximum dose: 15mg weekly.
seriousRisks: Thyroid C-cell tumors (observed in rodent studies; relevance to humans unknown)
Hypoglycemia (when used with insulin or sulfonylureas)
Acute kidney injury (from dehydration due to GI effects)
contraindications: Personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC)
Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia syndrome type 2 (MEN 2)
Known serious hypersensitivity to tirzepatide or any excipients
insuranceCoverage: Covered by many commercial plans for Type 2 Diabetes (Mounjaro). Zepbound coverage for weight management is expanding but remains inconsistent. Prior authorization typically required. Eli Lilly offers savings cards for eligible commercial patients.
clinicalTrials: SURMOUNT program (weight management: SURMOUNT-1 through SURMOUNT-4, MMO cardiovascular outcomes trial ongoing), SURPASS program (Type 2 Diabetes: SURPASS 1-5, SURPASS-CVOT)

keyResults.surmount1: 22.5% mean weight loss at 15mg vs 2.4% placebo over 72 weeks. 63% of participants achieved >=20% weight loss.
keyResults.surpass2: Superior A1C reduction vs semaglutide 1mg (-2.5% vs -1.9%)

keyAdvantages: Dual GLP-1/GIP mechanism produces greater weight loss than GLP-1 alone
Industry-leading weight loss results among approved medications (~22.5%)
Superior glycemic control vs semaglutide in head-to-head trials
Wide dose range allows individualized titration
keyDisadvantages: GI side effects during titration
Injection only (no oral formulation yet)
Supply shortages (though improving)
High cost without insurance
Less long-term safety data than semaglutide

name: Liraglutide
averageWeightLoss: ~8% body weight over 56 weeks at 3.0mg (SCALE Obesity trial). Approximately 5-6% at diabetes doses.
approvedFor: Saxenda: Weight Management; Victoza: Type 2 Diabetes
mechanism: Liraglutide is a GLP-1 analog with 97% homology to native human GLP-1. It binds to GLP-1 receptors to stimulate glucose-dependent insulin secretion, suppress glucagon, slow gastric emptying, and promote satiety via hypothalamic appetite centers. An acyl side chain enables albumin binding, extending its half-life compared to native GLP-1.
titrationSchedule: Saxenda: Start at 0.6mg daily for 1 week, increase by 0.6mg weekly until reaching 3.0mg daily maintenance dose. Victoza: Start at 0.6mg daily for 1 week, increase to 1.2mg, may increase to 1.8mg if needed.
seriousRisks: Thyroid C-cell tumors (observed in rodent studies; relevance to humans unknown)
Hypoglycemia (when combined with insulin or sulfonylureas)
contraindications: Personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC)
Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia syndrome type 2 (MEN 2)
Known hypersensitivity to liraglutide or any excipients
Pregnancy
insuranceCoverage: Victoza is commonly covered for Type 2 Diabetes. Saxenda coverage for weight management is limited; some commercial plans cover it with prior authorization. Medicare does not cover Saxenda.
clinicalTrials: SCALE program (weight management: SCALE Obesity, SCALE Diabetes, SCALE Maintenance, SCALE Sleep Apnea), LEADER trial (cardiovascular outcomes in diabetes)

keyResults.scaleObesity: 8.0% mean weight loss vs 2.6% placebo over 56 weeks. 33.1% achieved >=10% weight loss.
keyResults.leader: 13% reduction in major adverse cardiovascular events in Type 2 Diabetes

keyAdvantages: Longest track record of any GLP-1 for weight management (FDA approved 2014)
keyDisadvantages: Daily injection required (vs weekly for newer agents)
Lower weight loss compared to semaglutide and tirzepatide
Higher daily injection burden reduces adherence
Expensive for modest results compared to newer options
Being displaced by more effective weekly alternatives

name: Dulaglutide
averageWeightLoss: ~3-5% body weight (not FDA-approved for weight management; weight loss is a secondary benefit at diabetes doses)
mechanism: Dulaglutide consists of a GLP-1 analog covalently linked to a modified human IgG4 Fc fragment via a small peptide linker. This design reduces immunogenicity and slows clearance, enabling once-weekly dosing. It activates GLP-1 receptors to enhance glucose-dependent insulin secretion, suppress glucagon release, and slow gastric emptying.
titrationSchedule: Start at 0.75mg weekly for at least 4 weeks, increase to 1.5mg. If additional glycemic control needed, may increase to 3mg after at least 4 weeks, then to 4.5mg after at least 4 weeks.
seriousRisks: Thyroid C-cell tumors (observed in rodent studies; relevance to humans unknown)
Hypoglycemia (when used with insulin or sulfonylureas)
contraindications: Personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC)
Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia syndrome type 2 (MEN 2)
Known serious hypersensitivity to dulaglutide or any excipients
insuranceCoverage: Widely covered for Type 2 Diabetes by most commercial and Medicare Part D plans. Prior authorization may be required. Not approved or covered for weight management.
clinicalTrials: AWARD program (Type 2 Diabetes: AWARD 1-11), REWIND (cardiovascular outcomes trial)

keyResults.award1: Superior A1C reduction vs exenatide once weekly (-1.51% vs -0.99%)
keyResults.rewind: 12% reduction in major adverse cardiovascular events. Notable: enrolled lower CV risk population than other GLP-1 trials.

keyAdvantages: Once-weekly dosing with easy-to-use pre-filled pen
Hidden needle design reduces injection anxiety
keyDisadvantages: Not FDA-approved for weight management
Modest weight loss compared to semaglutide and tirzepatide
Less potent A1C reduction than tirzepatide
No oral formulation
Declining market share as newer agents gain coverage

name: Exenatide
averageWeightLoss: ~2-4% body weight (not FDA-approved for weight management; weight loss is a secondary benefit)
approvedFor: Byetta: Type 2 Diabetes (twice daily); Bydureon: Type 2 Diabetes (once weekly)
mechanism: Exenatide is a synthetic version of exendin-4, a peptide originally discovered in the saliva of the Gila monster (Heloderma suspectum). It shares 53% homology with human GLP-1 and is resistant to degradation by DPP-4 enzyme. It activates GLP-1 receptors to stimulate glucose-dependent insulin secretion, suppress glucagon, slow gastric emptying, and promote satiety. Bydureon uses microsphere technology for sustained release.
dosingSchedule: Twice daily (Byetta) or Once weekly (Bydureon BCise)
titrationSchedule: Byetta: Start at 5mcg twice daily (within 60 minutes before morning and evening meals) for at least 1 month, then may increase to 10mcg twice daily. Bydureon: 2mg once weekly, no titration required.
commonSideEffects: Injection site reactions (especially Bydureon: nodules, pruritus)
seriousRisks: Thyroid C-cell tumors (observed in rodent studies with extended-release; relevance to humans unknown)
contraindications: Personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC) (Bydureon only)
Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia syndrome type 2 (MEN 2) (Bydureon only)
Known hypersensitivity to exenatide or any excipients
Severe renal impairment (eGFR <30) or end-stage renal disease
insuranceCoverage: Generally covered for Type 2 Diabetes. May face step therapy requirements (try metformin first). Coverage has declined as newer GLP-1 agents have gained market share.
halfLife: ~2.4 hours (Byetta); extended release over weeks (Bydureon microspheres)
clinicalTrials: EXSCEL (cardiovascular outcomes trial), DURATION program (extended-release studies 1-8)

keyResults.exscel: Did not reach statistical significance for MACE reduction (HR 0.91, p=0.06), but showed non-inferiority for cardiovascular safety
keyResults.duration5: Bydureon showed superior A1C reduction vs Byetta twice daily (-1.6% vs -0.9%)

keyAdvantages: Bydureon BCise is a simple autoinjector with no mixing
Available as generic in some markets
keyDisadvantages: Twice daily dosing (Byetta) is burdensome
Least weight loss among GLP-1 class
Injection site nodules with Bydureon
Failed to demonstrate significant cardiovascular benefit
Largely superseded by more effective agents
Contraindicated in severe renal impairment

name: Survodutide
averageWeightLoss: ~19% body weight over 46 weeks at 4.8mg in Phase 2 trial. Phase 3 SYNCHRONIZE trials ongoing with 6.0mg dose.
approvedFor: Pending FDA approval: Weight Management / MASH
mechanism: Survodutide is a dual agonist that activates both GLP-1 and glucagon receptors. GLP-1 activation reduces appetite, slows gastric emptying, and improves insulin secretion. Glucagon receptor activation increases energy expenditure, promotes hepatic fat oxidation, and enhances lipolysis. The combination aims to produce greater weight loss than GLP-1 alone by both reducing caloric intake and increasing caloric expenditure. The glucagon component also targets liver fat reduction, making it promising for MASH (metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis).
titrationSchedule: Phase 3 trial protocol: Start at 0.6mg weekly, titrate up every 4 weeks through 2.4mg, 3.6mg, 4.8mg to a maintenance dose of 6.0mg weekly (titration period approximately 20 weeks).
seriousRisks: GI side effects leading to dehydration
Full safety profile still under investigation
contraindications: Not yet approved — contraindications will be determined through regulatory review
Likely to include MTC/MEN 2 history (consistent with GLP-1 class)
insuranceCoverage: Not yet applicable. Expected to seek FDA approval for both obesity and MASH indications.
clinicalTrials: SYNCHRONIZE program: SYNCHRONIZE-1 (obesity without diabetes), SYNCHRONIZE-2 (obesity with Type 2 Diabetes), SYNCHRONIZE-3 (MASH with fibrosis). Phase 2 results published in NEJM (2024).

keyResults.phase2Obesity: Up to 19.0% weight loss at 4.8mg over 46 weeks vs 2.1% placebo. 44% of participants lost >=20% body weight.
keyResults.phase2MASH: Up to 83% MASH resolution rate (vs 18.2% placebo) in Phase 2b MASH trial

keyAdvantages: Dual mechanism increases energy expenditure (not just appetite suppression)
Strong MASH/liver fat reduction data — unique among GLP-1 class
Competitive weight loss approaching tirzepatide levels
Addresses metabolic liver disease — large unmet need
keyDisadvantages: Not yet FDA approved
Glucagon activation may raise blood glucose (offsetting GLP-1 glucose-lowering)
GI side effects appear comparable to other GLP-1 agents
Long titration period (~20 weeks to max dose)
Limited long-term safety data

name: Orforglipron
averageWeightLoss: ~14.7% body weight over 36 weeks at 45mg in Phase 2 trial. Phase 3 ACHIEVE program ongoing with longer duration expected to show greater loss.
averageCost: Pricing not yet established; expected to be significantly lower than injectable GLP-1s due to simpler manufacturing (brand); Non-peptide molecule may be harder to compound (compounded)
approvedFor: Pending FDA approval: Weight Management / Type 2 Diabetes
mechanism: Orforglipron is a first-in-class oral non-peptide GLP-1 receptor agonist. Unlike oral semaglutide (Rybelsus), which is a peptide requiring absorption enhancers and fasting, orforglipron is a small molecule that activates GLP-1 receptors with high potency. It stimulates glucose-dependent insulin secretion, suppresses glucagon, slows gastric emptying, and reduces appetite — the same mechanisms as injectable GLP-1 agents but in a more convenient oral form without fasting requirements.
titrationSchedule: Phase 3 protocol: Start at 3mg daily, increase every 4 weeks through 6mg, 12mg, 24mg, 36mg to maintenance dose of 45mg daily. Total titration period approximately 20 weeks.
seriousRisks: GI side effects (most common reason for discontinuation in Phase 2)
Thyroid C-cell tumors (theoretical class risk, being evaluated)
Full safety profile still under investigation
contraindications: Not yet approved — contraindications will be determined through regulatory review
Likely to include MTC/MEN 2 history (consistent with GLP-1 class)

typicalMonthlyCost.brand: Pricing not yet established; expected to be significantly lower than injectable GLP-1s due to simpler manufacturing
typicalMonthlyCost.compounded: Non-peptide molecule may be harder to compound

insuranceCoverage: Not yet applicable. Oral formulation expected to improve access and potentially lower costs vs injectables.
clinicalTrials: ACHIEVE program: ACHIEVE-1 (obesity/overweight), ACHIEVE-2 (Type 2 Diabetes), ACHIEVE-3 (obesity with Type 2 Diabetes), ACHIEVE-4 (cardiovascular outcomes). Phase 2 results published in NEJM (2023).

keyResults.phase2Obesity: 14.7% body weight reduction at 45mg over 36 weeks vs 2.3% placebo
keyResults.phase2Diabetes: 2.1% A1C reduction at 45mg over 26 weeks vs 0.4% placebo

keyAdvantages: Small molecule — simpler, cheaper manufacturing than peptides
Could dramatically expand GLP-1 access and lower costs
keyDisadvantages: Not yet FDA approved
GI side effect rates similar to injectable GLP-1s
Daily dosing (vs weekly injection)
Weight loss may be less than tirzepatide at current doses
Limited long-term data
Higher discontinuation rates in trials vs injectable GLP-1s

name: Retatrutide
averageWeightLoss: ~24.2% body weight over 48 weeks at 12mg in Phase 2 trial. The highest responding group showed up to 26.3% weight loss. Phase 3 TRIUMPH program may show even greater results over longer duration.
approvedFor: Pending FDA approval: Weight Management / Type 2 Diabetes
mechanism: Retatrutide is a first-in-class triple incretin agonist that simultaneously activates three receptors: GLP-1 (appetite suppression, insulin secretion), GIP (enhanced insulin sensitivity, fat metabolism), and glucagon (increased energy expenditure, hepatic fat oxidation). This triple mechanism addresses obesity through three complementary pathways: reducing caloric intake (GLP-1), improving metabolic efficiency (GIP), and increasing caloric expenditure (glucagon). The combination has produced the highest weight loss of any anti-obesity medication studied to date.
titrationSchedule: Phase 2 protocol: Start at 0.5mg weekly, titrate through 1mg, 2mg, 4mg, 8mg to 12mg weekly over approximately 20 weeks with dose increases every 4 weeks. Phase 3 titration schedules being finalized.
seriousRisks: Thyroid C-cell tumors (theoretical class risk, being evaluated)
Potential hyperglycemic effect from glucagon agonism (under investigation)
Full safety profile still under investigation
contraindications: Not yet approved — contraindications will be determined through regulatory review
Likely to include MTC/MEN 2 history (consistent with GLP-1/GIP class)
insuranceCoverage: Not yet applicable. Expected to seek FDA approval for obesity and potentially Type 2 Diabetes and MASH.
clinicalTrials: TRIUMPH program: TRIUMPH-1 (obesity/overweight without diabetes), TRIUMPH-2 (obesity with Type 2 Diabetes), TRIUMPH-3 (MASH), TRIUMPH-4 (cardiovascular outcomes). Phase 2 results published in NEJM (2023).

keyResults.phase2: 24.2% mean weight loss at 12mg over 48 weeks vs 2.1% placebo. 26% achieved >=30% body weight loss. Participants with obesity and Type 2 Diabetes lost up to 17.5%.

keyAdvantages: Highest weight loss of any anti-obesity medication studied (~24%)
Potential MASH indication (glucagon component reduces liver fat)
Could redefine treatment expectations for obesity
Phase 2 results suggest Phase 3 may show 25-30% weight loss
keyDisadvantages: Not yet FDA approved (likely 2027+ at earliest)
Furthest from market of pipeline candidates
GI side effects comparable to dual agonists
Glucagon component complexity (potential hyperglycemia in diabetics)
Limited safety data — only Phase 2 completed
Injection only
